item.title: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded: I am unable to delete this Post from the IRC. You should do so if you can. I won't be pursuing this anymore.

item.title: Re: Licensing Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Well, you have completely crushed my dreams.

So it goes. I suppose I will survive.

On the bright side, SCP readers will not not be distracted by my mediocre writing attempts.

Truly, SCP Foundation has become the soulless, mindless, bureaucratic machine it presents itself to be in fiction. I suppose that was the goal. Congratulations and best of luck to you all.

item.title: Re: Species VX
item.content:encoded: I've read the SCP and it is confusing since at one moment you are speaking about vampire-child and another about a virus breakout. Other than that background feels more like a tale than actual research by the foundation since you are using 1st person type of narration. There is also no hard evidence that aliens had created a virus. And finally, you stated in a critique that the child had killed agents but in the article, it's said that it's immobile My suggestion is to make separate SCPS one virus and another vampire, and make the background feel more like research. Word formatting and grammar is great, the same goes for containment procedures for the vampire.

item.title: Re: Species VX
item.content:encoded:
Maybe I did a poor job of summarizing. I am dropping a few balls of yarn on the floor and letting them roll. If people like this first bit, I will build on it, if not then back to the drawing board.

I am unaware of Pentagram. The CIA "Special Activities Division" is real.

Please give it a read and thumbs or down. Thank you.

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/species-vx

item.title: Re: Species VX
item.content:encoded: The SCP just doesn't feel like it has a connection since you are in one sentence talking about a vampire-like specimen and in another about a virus. I think you should pick one and go with it. Also, you didn't develop the story enough. What evidence does the foundation have to know that its alien species? Where was it discovered? How was it discovered? You should try answering some of these questions to give the SCP proper background.

item.title: Re: Licensing Staff Notice
item.content:encoded:
My art is mine to do with as I wish. The Youtube channel is mine as well. The videos I have made. I am completely unencumbered.

I am a bit confused. The SCP article that brought me here contained an image of art made by a Japanese artist who gave his permission for use of the image on this site.

I can give myself permission for use of my art here as well, right?

If the purpose of demanding Creative Commons licensing is to prevent copyright infringement, then there is nothing to worry about. I can prove the media is mine. I already own the channel and I have no desire to create another using Wikidot.

It would be helpful if you read the SCP I have already written.

The Tianzhong facility is a real place. I have access to it. I can use it as a set for making movies. I have no intention of releasing video material under the Creative Commons.

Perhaps I do not belong here, or maybe I just don't understand. Why wouldn't I be permitted to link to my own IP using my own web-hosting site so I can retain my copyrights for my video material?

item.title: Re: Species VX
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Evidence of an Alien race attempting to augment the rabies virus with nanobots. Alien psychological warfare is implied. A vampire-like creature has been created from an alien experiment gone awry.

I'm not exactly sure how these three things are tied together: it kinda feels like three unrelated alien plots over a single SCP with various facets to me?

I think this is my largest concern with your pitch actually: you've oversummarised everything to the point where I don't really have a clear idea of how stuff flows together, like consider:

A failed alien experiment produced a vampire-like human(?) three year old male child which attacked a CIA operative on assignment in Taiwan. A schism between CIA Special Activities Division and the Foundation is created.

How is this schism created? Where does the Foundation fit in here? How is the 'CIA Special Activities Division' different from 'Pentagram'?

If I was to summarise how I feel about this, 'unsure' would be the word I'd choose: I don't feel like I have a good enough picture of how this all fits together to actually say anything meaningful here.

item.title: Licensing Staff Notice
item.content:encoded:
First of all, media on the wiki, whether it be images or videos, must be under a Creative Commons license. While we offer some leeway for stuff that is just linked and is hosted offsite, you must make it clear that that content is not under the site's license. An example that comes to mind is 248-J.

In this scenario, however, because of the volume of videos you'll be using in your piece and how they appear to be significantly important to your piece, I will ask as a member of the Licensing Team that you do not do such a thing unless you explicitly release those videos under a CC BY-SA 3.0 compliant license. As it's unknown how important those 37 videos of yours will be to the narrative of your article, I am forced to prohibit linking them unless you are either willing to release the videos under a Creative Commons license, or can state that their inclusion is not central to the article itself.

If you intend to release the videos under Creative Commons, you can alternatively look into options for hosting videos on Wikidot instead of linking to your channel.

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.
